checks: The attained denominator is positive on K and has the stated first moment. The positive projective map preserves all translated central halfspace signs and has Jacobian L^(−d−1), so the image is compact convex of centroid zero.
The tangent continuation of t^(−d) is positive, finite and convex on the full line. Its product by the positive centered support gives a jointly continuous field convex at each normal.

The divergence of (x−c)L^(−d) is dL^(−d−1). A through-c clipping plane has zero new flux, and its intersection with the old boundary is surface-null because it cuts the interior. The old-boundary integral is d times the transformed cap volume. The uncut total is d times the transformed volume, including the endpoint case.
The centroid theorem applies to the transformed convex body. Enlarging to the original closed containing trace can only increase the positive boundary contribution, including full traces.

The affine base penalties are zero at their paying endpoint and strictly negative at every other sampled base. Compactness gives a uniform B making the positive-part field vanish on the other sampled boundaries. Each denominator is positive, and summing normalized fields leaves nonnegative cross payments.
